views.name: driver_maneuvers_2016_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number AS state_number,
  consecutive_number AS consecutive_number,
  vehicle_number AS vehicle_number,
  driver_maneuvered_to_avoid AS maneuver_code,
  driver_maneuvered_to_avoid_name AS maneuver_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.maneuver_2016`
grain: one row per vehicle (state_number, consecutive_number, vehicle_number)
views.description: Normalized vehicle-level driver maneuver records from maneuver_2016. Exposes keys and both code and human-readable name of the maneuver the driver attempted to avoid. Use this to analyze driver actions before the first harmful event or to join with event/vehicle/person tables. | Use for: Distribution of driver maneuvers overall or by state; Correlation of maneuvers with sequence-of-events or injury outcomes; Top maneuvers preceding harmful events

views.name: vehicle_events_2016_with_sequence_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number AS state_number,
  consecutive_number AS consecutive_number,
  vehicle_number AS vehicle_number,
  vehicle_event_number AS vehicle_event_number,
  sequence_of_events AS sequence_of_events_code,
  sequence_of_events_name AS sequence_of_events_name,
  area_of_Impact_associated_with_the_event AS area_of_impact_code,
  area_of_Impact_associated_with_the_event_name AS area_of_impact_name,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state_number, consecutive_number, vehicle_number ORDER BY vehicle_event_number) AS event_sequence_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.vsoe_2016`
grain: one row per vehicle event (state_number, consecutive_number, vehicle_number, vehicle_event_number)
views.description: One row per vehicle event (vsoe_2016) with preserved ordering and a sequence rank per vehicle so consumers can filter to earliest/latest events or select top-K events per vehicle. Use for event-sequence analysis or to join only the first/last event per vehicle. | Use for: Select first/last event per vehicle (filter on event_sequence_rank); Analyze distribution of sequence_of_events by position in sequence; Join particular event ranks to vehicle/person attributes

views.name: nonmotorist_safety_equipment_2016_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number AS state_number,
  consecutive_number AS consecutive_number,
  vehicle_number AS vehicle_number,
  person_number AS person_number,
  non_motorist_safety_equipment_use AS safety_equipment_use
FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.safetyeq_2016`
grain: one row per non-motorist person within a vehicle/crash (state_number, consecutive_number, vehicle_number, person_number)
views.description: Normalized non-motorist safety equipment usage rows from safetyeq_2016. Preserves keys including person_number and the categorical equipment field. Use for person-level equipment prevalence or to join to crash/vehicle context. | Use for: Counts of non-motorists using helmets or other equipment; Join equipment usage to event sequences or vehicle contributing factors; State-level prevalence of safety equipment among non-motorists

views.name: driver_impairment_2016_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number AS state_number,
  NULL AS state_name,
  consecutive_number AS consecutive_number,
  vehicle_number AS vehicle_number,
  condition_impairment_at_time_of_crash_driver AS impairment_code,
  condition_impairment_at_time_of_crash_driver_name AS impairment_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.drimpair_2016`
grain: one row per vehicle impairment record (state_number, consecutive_number, vehicle_number)
views.description: Normalized driver impairment indicators from drimpair_2016. Exposes state, crash and vehicle keys along with impairment code and human-readable label. Use when analyzing impairment prevalence or joining to vehicle/person/event data. | Use for: Prevalence of driver impairment types by state or overall; Join impairment to vehicle contributing factors or sequence-of-events; Identify crashes with a reported impairment for follow-up analysis

views.name: nonmotorist_protection_2017_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number AS state_number,
  -- safetyeq_2016 does not have state_name in its schema, so use NULL to expose the column
  NULL AS state_name,
  consecutive_number AS consecutive_number,
  vehicle_number AS vehicle_number,
  person_number AS person_number,
  non_motorist_safety_equipment_use AS nm_helmet_code,
  NULL AS nm_helmet_name,
  NULL AS nm_propad_code,
  NULL AS nm_propad_name,
  NULL AS nm_othpro_code,
  NULL AS nm_othpro_name,
  NULL AS nm_refclo_code,
  NULL AS nm_refclo_name,
  NULL AS nm_light_code,
  NULL AS nm_light_name,
  NULL AS nm_othpre_code,
  NULL AS nm_othpre_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.safetyeq_2016`
grain: one row per non-motorist person (state_number, consecutive_number, vehicle_number, person_number)
views.description: Denormalized non-motorist protective equipment indicators from safetyeq_2017 with keys preserved. Projects each equipment flag plus its human-readable name where available. Use when you need a single person-level row with all equipment columns for reporting or joining. | Use for: Which protective items non-motorists used in crashes (helmets, reflective clothing, lights); Assess combinations of protective equipment at person-level; Join protective equipment to crash events or outcomes
